builder_plan.scenario: An agent reads external documents or tool responses that may contain malicious instructions.
builder_plan.change: Replay attacks and legitimate lookalikes in an isolated copy of your agent workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your existing checks with the same tasks, permissions, and tool responses.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful attacks missed, legitimate actions blocked, detection delay, and review cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Antidistillation is Cheap: Lightweight Distillation-Resistance via Stylistic Corruption
summary: The method replaces surrogate-model next-token sampling defenses with lightweight activation-level style-steering vectors injected only on suspected malicious queries. It costs a small inference-time intervention and activation-space engineering rather than a separate surrogate model, with negligible claimed latency overhead. It can fail if malicious queries are misclassified, if style steering degrades semantic utility or fluency in practice, or if the defense proves sensitive to model and workload specifics.
rationale: The approach is relevant to API protection but depends on activation access and validation in the reader's exact deployment setting, so it is not yet an obvious production default.

claims.statement: The method replaces surrogate-model next-token sampling defenses with lightweight activation-level style-steering vectors injected only on suspected malicious queries. It costs a small inference-time intervention and activation-space engineering rather than a separate surrogate model, with negligible claimed latency overhead. It can fail if malicious queries are misclassified, if style steering degrades semantic utility or fluency in practice, or if the defense proves sensitive to model and workload specifics.
Substantial anti-distillation performance with negligible overhead and preserved text naturalness; no multiplicative factor is reported in the abstract.
